hypothesis: In B. rossi babesiosis, a higher circulating monocyte count at admission goes with more severe disease, beyond anaemia and total leukocytes.
evidence: T02: 4 of 4 B. rossi sources in the expected direction (DS05 monocytes with dullness rho +0.45, partial +0.29 after haematocrit, WBC, segmented and band neutrophils and illness days; S-CB517 died +0.25; DS07 CD14 +0.42, halves after haemoglobin beta; Beagles +0.67), Stouffer q 0.00016 over 8 themes; but without DS05, the source that suggested it, Z 2.31 (Bonferroni 0.084). Monocyte count does not track MCP-1
human_counterpart: Monocyte/macrophage markers with severity: soluble CD14 with severity in falciparum malaria and presepsin (sCD14-ST) higher in sepsis non-survivors agree; MCP-1 independently prognostic in sepsis; but monocyte activation markers were lower in severe malaria in Malawian children and MCP-1 lower in complicated falciparum malaria (mixed)
parallel_new: partly: the CCL2 (MCP-1) parallel is made in CB017, CB517, CB107; a circulating monocyte count or sCD14 parallel was not found in a CB text
refuted_by: No monocyte-count difference by outcome in a non-Onderstepoort B. rossi cohort with a hard outcome, or a difference that disappears after WBC and haematocrit adjustment
next_study_existing_data: Monocyte count and monocyte fraction against death in the probable DS03-S-CB050 join is not possible (DS03 has no leukocytes); cheapest: ask the CB040 authors (320 B. rossi dogs, SV-02c request) for dog-level monocyte counts and outcome
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 prospective B. rossi cohort with at least 200 dogs outside Onderstepoort: admission CBC with differential, outcome components stored separately
minimum_dataset_addition: Manual or analyser differential with absolute monocyte count; plasma sCD14 (presepsin) and CCL2 on stored pre-treatment plasma

hypothesis: Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular trap release (cfDNA, nucleosomes, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin) are greater in severe B. rossi babesiosis, beyond neutrophil number.
evidence: Gap: never measured in canine babesiosis (CB107 states NETosis is unstudied). Weak, confounded support: DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (q 0.29), a third explained by haemoglobin beta; histone H4 untestable; Beagle granule transcripts rose in all 5 dogs with no severity gradient
human_counterpart: Plasma elastase and MPO higher in cerebral malaria; circulating histones raised with brain swelling in cerebral malaria; neutrophil granule transcripts associated with severe malaria and with sepsis mortality; but cfDNA and MPO-DNA did not predict death after adjustment in a sepsis cohort (mixed)
parallel_new: yes for NETs, histones, calprotectin and released MPO/elastase (only speculated in CB articles); band neutrophils and MPXI are published
refuted_by: Plasma cfDNA, nucleosomes or calprotectin no higher in dogs that die once the band neutrophil count is adjusted for
next_study_existing_data: Re-quantify DS06 from SRA PRJNA703846 without the CPM filter to recover MPO and ELANE (a coordinator decision, large download); no severity contrast in those 5 dogs
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: citrate plasma (not serum) for cfDNA by fluorometry and calprotectin; nucleosome ELISA only with a haemolysis and icterus check
minimum_dataset_addition: Plasma cfDNA, calprotectin (S100A8/A9), plasma MPO and elastase; band and segmented neutrophil counts

hypothesis: More intravascular haemolysis per unit of anaemia (cell-free haemoglobin and haem load relative to haematocrit and scavenger capacity) goes with severe and fatal B. rossi disease, as in severe falciparum and knowlesi malaria and sepsis.
evidence: Gap: no CB article relates measured cell-free haemoglobin or haem to outcome. Existing data do not support it: DS07 haemoglobin beta +0.48 (q 0.133) partly restates the label and moves with another red-cell protein (sample haemolysis not excluded); the Beagle cfHb contrast is parasite load, already reported (CB082)
human_counterpart: Cell-free haemoglobin higher with AKI in severe falciparum malaria, with death in Ugandan children (with low haemopexin), with severity in knowlesi malaria, and independently with death in sepsis
parallel_new: partly: CB119 proposes cfHb as a severity measure without data; no quantified canine cfHb-outcome study
refuted_by: No difference in cfHb (or cfHb per haematocrit unit, or haemopexin depletion) between dogs that die and survive in a cohort that measures a sample haemolysis index
next_study_existing_data: None adequate: DS07 lacks haematocrit, bilirubin and a haemolysis index. Cheapest is stored pre-treatment plasma (CB145 / Onderstepoort biobank, SV-02c-type request)
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: plasma cfHb by spectrophotometry with haematocrit, haptoglobin, haemopexin and a haemolysis index at admission
minimum_dataset_addition: Plasma cell-free haemoglobin, haemolysis index, haptoglobin, haemopexin; urine haemoglobin

hypothesis: Endothelial activation measured as plasma angiopoietin-2 is higher in dogs with severe or fatal B. rossi babesiosis.
evidence: Gap: never measured in canine babesiosis (0 CB notes or texts, 1 PubMed record not about Ang-2). Not in DS07; DS06 holds no ANGPT2 transcript. The Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio is not assayable in dogs with the validated kit, so the lead is Ang-2 alone
human_counterpart: Ang-2 rose with severity in all 11 falciparum studies of a systematic review and discriminated death (AUROC 0.71 to 0.83); higher in sepsis non-survivors (meta-analysis); in canine SIRS and sepsis higher in non-survivors
parallel_new: yes: no CB article makes it
refuted_by: No Ang-2 difference between dogs that die and survive once haemolysis and creatinine are accounted for
next_study_existing_data: None in the public files. Stored pre-treatment plasma with outcome (Onderstepoort biobank; contacting the authors is a user decision)
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: plasma Ang-2 at admission with creatinine and a haemolysis index
minimum_dataset_addition: Plasma angiopoietin-2 (validated canine ELISA), stored EDTA or citrate plasma at -80 C

hypothesis: VWF release and ADAMTS13 consumption (a higher VWF:ADAMTS13 ratio) go with severe B. rossi babesiosis and its microthrombi.
evidence: Gap: CB145 measured factor activities, fibrinolysis and microthrombi at necropsy by outcome, but not VWF or ADAMTS13; CB446 found vWF activity lower than in controls in 12 dogs without an outcome contrast, so the direction cannot be assumed. Coagulation theme T05 null (1 of 3)
human_counterpart: Higher VWF and ultra-large multimers with lower ADAMTS13 in severe and cerebral falciparum malaria (small cohorts); VWF in malaria-associated ARDS
parallel_new: yes for the severity link; CB446 measured vWF against controls only
refuted_by: VWF antigen, VWF activity and ADAMTS13 activity the same in dogs that die and survive, or VWF lower in severe dogs as CB446's direction suggests
next_study_existing_data: None public. CB145 cohort plasma (thromboinflammation study, raw data on request) is the natural place to add VWF and ADAMTS13
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: citrate plasma for VWF antigen, VWF:collagen binding and ADAMTS13 activity
minimum_dataset_addition: Citrate plasma: VWF antigen, VWF activity, ADAMTS13 activity; platelet count

hypothesis: Hyperferritinaemia (macrophage activation and iron sequestration) at admission goes with severe or fatal B. rossi babesiosis.
evidence: Gap: the only canine babesiosis ferritin data are 7 infected vs 7 healthy dogs (CB242, no severity contrast, species not identified) and one case report. Not in DS07 or any tidy file. Confounded in a haemolytic disease by iron release and the acute-phase response
human_counterpart: Ferritin higher in sepsis non-survivors in several large cohorts; very high ferritin marks a macrophage-activation-like phenotype in septic shock; in malaria ferritin rises with clinical infection but is confounded by inflammation (an infection contrast, not severity)
parallel_new: yes: no CB article makes it
refuted_by: No ferritin difference by outcome once CRP and a haemolysis marker (cell-free haemoglobin or bilirubin) are adjusted for
next_study_existing_data: None public; stored serum with outcome (same biobank question as the other plasma leads)
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: serum ferritin with CRP, serum iron and transferrin at admission
minimum_dataset_addition: Serum ferritin (canine immunoassay), with CRP, serum iron, transferrin and a haemolysis marker

hypothesis: Higher kynurenine:tryptophan (IDO activity) at admission goes with severe or fatal canine babesiosis.
evidence: Gap: kynurenine was measured only against healthy dogs (CB091 serum, B. canis: kynurenine and Kyn/Trp clearly higher in infected dogs, no severity label). The nearest severity proxy (CB071 urine, renal-function groups, 5 to 10 dogs per group) is null. CB071, CB091 and CB137 are one cohort (CH06)
human_counterpart: Higher IDO activity (kynurenine:tryptophan) and kynurenine with sepsis severity and death; CSF kynurenine pathway metabolites with longer coma in cerebral malaria (mostly cerebral, not systemic, evidence in malaria)
parallel_new: yes for severity; the infection contrast is published (CB091)
refuted_by: No Kyn/Trp difference by outcome once creatinine (azotaemia) and CRP are adjusted for
next_study_existing_data: None public with a severity label; the CB091 supplement has dog-level values but no severity label (ask the authors for complicated status: a user decision)
next_study_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: plasma tryptophan and kynurenine by LC-MS/MS with creatinine and CRP
minimum_dataset_addition: Plasma tryptophan, kynurenine (LC-MS/MS); creatinine and CRP for adjustment
